e: From Middle English aulnage, from Old French alnage, aulnage (modern French aunage), from alne (“ell”), of Germanic origin: compare Old High German elina, Gothic 𐌰𐌻𐌴𐌹𐌽𐌰 (aleina, “cubit”). See ell.
q:
Poets and kings are but the clerks of Time,
 Tiering the same dull webs of discontent,
 Clipping the same sad alnage of the years.

e: From the chemical symbols Al, Ni and Co.
